decision.initial_reason: Connecticut required 39 second-half points to clear 75.5 and showed strong positive shooting-regression indicators after a 3-for-17 second quarter and 2-for-14 first-half three-point shooting.
decision.pivot_trigger: CON team total moved from 75.5 to 77.5 while NYL team total remained 89.5, materially compressing the Connecticut edge while preserving the New York under edge.

notes: The final NYL team total of 82 finished 7.5 points below the wager line of 89.5, producing a clean win.

The original Connecticut Over 75.5 would also have lost by 0.5 points; after the market move to 77.5 it would have lost by 2.5 points. The derivative pivot therefore both preserved value and avoided the original losing position.
SharpEdge overestimated the absolute second-half scoring level by 8 points, projecting 82 remaining points versus 74 actual.

Despite that level error, the allocation layer was directionally exact: SharpEdge projected Connecticut to outscore New York by 2 in the second half, and Connecticut actually won the second half 38-36.
The pre-market spread fair line of NYL -7 matched the final 82-75 margin exactly.
This result supports separating total-level calibration from team-share allocation and supports rescanning correlated derivatives when a preferred line is steamed toward fair value.
